answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust with random walks of at most \(t\) steps from independently trusted seeds. If a sybil cluster—whether labeled knoll, grove, or opal—has low conductance, only a small fraction of walk probability can cross its sparse external cut per step. Thus its reachable trust, and hence voting weight, is bounded by seed access and roughly \(t\) times the cut ratio; min-cut bounds prevent transitive attestations from amplifying that mass without limit.
